To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the As(III) concentration in groundwater discharging from an aquifer to a coastal embayment is determined by the redox conditions of the groundwater plume, and the sorption capacity and Kd of the aquifer sediment.

(i) Fe(III) in groundwater is oxidized and precipitates in sediments as water flows toward a bay, and this results in precipitation of As to the Fe(III) oxide coatings; (ii) As is oxidized and adsorbed to Fe(III) precipitates at redox interfaces; (iii) the amount of Fe(III)/Fe in sediment controls sorption capacity of Fe(III); and (iv) a SCM is more accurate than a Kd
(i) the As concentration in groundwater is controlled by the redox interface and (ii) the As concentration is controlled by Fe(III) in sediments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fate and transport of arsenic in the environment.
the geochemical controls on As transport in a coastal aquifers.
the fate of arsenic in groundwater in a reducing aquifer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the As transport is controlled by coupled hydrologic and chemical processes.
As(III) adsorption is strongly controlled by the redox state and Fe(III) content of the sediment and is best described by a SCM.
As(III) oxidation and adsorption to Fe(III) oxide surfaces are coupled to hydrological flow and are key processes controlling As transport to the bay.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
reactive transport of As is controlled by coupled control of chemistry (Fe redox) and hydrology.
the chemistry of As in the Waquoit Bay aquifer is controlled by the coupled hydrology and geochemistry, which in turn control the reactive transport of As. (C) 2008 Elsevier B.V. All

The main takeaway from our work is that
reactive transport of As is controlled by coupled chemistry-hydrology.
the chemistry of As in groundwater at Waquoit is controlled by Fe(III)-Fe(II) reduction and As(III)-As(V) redox cycling.
the coupled control of hydrology and chemistry on the reactive transport of groundwater As is a key factor to consider in assessing the potential for As contamination of coastal groundwater.
